rule_summary: Follows PA statewide Chapter 75 caps/fees with no size/fee deviation. Export credit (annual true-up) valued at PECO's Price-to-Compare, ~11.0-11.8 cents/kWh as of Q1-Q2 2026 (fluctuates with PUC-approved default service procurement). PUC's 2022-2024 interconnection report flags PECO as having a disproportionate number of Level 1->Level 2 upgrades (141 in 2024) due to antiquated low-voltage distribution circuits in parts of its territory -- expect engineering-study kickbacks on Level 1 applications more often than other PA EDCs.
storage_specific_notes: Largest PA EDC by interconnection volume (25,252 cumulative Tier I interconnections through 2024, 2nd behind PPL); mean Level 2 review time ~21 days (2024), roughly in line with statutory targets but circuit-upgrade kickbacks add delay for a meaningful subset of projects.

rule_summary: Follows PA statewide Chapter 75 caps/fees with no size/fee deviation. Export credit valued at PPL's Price-to-Compare, ~13.0 cents/kWh as of Q2 2026. PPL is the largest PA EDC by customer-generator count (25,252 as of 2024) and has the fastest, most automated Level 1 review process among major PA EDCs (mean ~1 business day in 2022-2024, well under the 25-business-day statutory cap) -- notably favorable for fast Level 1 (<=10kW) BESS-attached PV interconnection.
storage_specific_notes: PPL explicitly requires UL 1741 Supplement B / IEEE 1547-2018 certified inverters. Fastest Level 1 turnaround of any major PA EDC by a wide margin.

rule_summary: Follows PA statewide Chapter 75 caps/fees. Export credit valued at Met-Ed's Price-to-Compare, ~13.0 cents/kWh as of Q2 2026. storage_specific_notes: PUC's 2022-2024 interconnection report documents Met-Ed approving battery retrofits onto existing net-metered solar (e.g., 2 requests in 2024 approved to add a 10kW battery to an existing solar PV interconnection, moved from Level 1 to Level 2 review) -- confirms PA/Met-Ed permits storage-only retrofit additions to a legacy net-metered PV system without disqualifying the existing interconnection, though the addition itself gets re-reviewed at the higher level triggered by combined capacity.

Export credit valued at Duquesne's Price-to-Compare, ~13.75-14.1 cents/kWh as of Q1-Q2 2026 (highest PTC among major PA EDCs, favorable for NEM economics but also the benchmark rate for default-service Hourly SOS customers). storage_specific_notes: Duquesne also offers Default Service Hourly Pricing (Hourly SOS) for large C&I customers -- an hourly LMP-indexed passthrough rate that is directly relevant to storage arbitrage economics on the import side, separate from NEM export credit.

rule_summary: Small FirstEnergy-adjacent-style electric-only division (UGI's core business is natural gas; electric service territories are limited pockets in northeastern/central PA). Follows PA statewide Chapter 75 rules but is a minor EDC with a small interconnection volume (82 customer-generators as of 2024, smallest major reporting EDC alongside Wellsboro/Pike/Citizens). rule_summary: PSC-regulated IOU; nonresidential net-metering cap is 2 MW per meter at Delmarva (vs. 500 kW per meter at DEC or a DEMEC municipal utility) -- Delmarva DE customers get a materially larger nonresidential system-size ceiling than co-op/muni customers in the state. Residential 25kW cap and annual-expiry true-up (per SB 298, 2022) apply as state default. Also administers Delaware's statewide Green Energy Program (established 1999, funded via a per-kWh surcharge on Delmarva customers) which has awarded >$55M in grants for renewable/storage-adjacent projects since inception -- separate from net metering and worth surfacing to Delmarva-territory customers evaluating a design.
storage_specific_notes: Delmarva publishes its own interconnection guidelines and battery-storage-specific interconnection documentation separate from DEC's forms; grid-charging/non-export provisions not independently confirmed this pass.

rule_summary: DEC is a member-owned cooperative and is NOT bound by PSC-adopted net metering/interconnection regulations -- it promulgates its own rules per 26 Del. C. Section 1014's direction that cooperatives set their own. DEC's nonresidential cap is 500 kW per meter (vs 2 MW at Delmarva). DEC requires a separate supplemental Battery Storage Interconnection Application in addition to the base Interconnection Application whenever a battery is added alongside a generating system -- distinct paperwork track from solar-only net metering. DEC has separate agreement forms for Net Metering (>100kW), Non-Export (<100kW), and Battery Storage, implying DEC treats sub-100kW systems as non-export by default absent net-metering election -- verify this reading against the actual agreement text. Implementation history: DEC initially set its post-SB-298 annualized billing period to end in December with no final credit payout, which caused customer/legislator backlash (particularly among large-payout farm net-metering customers); DEC then moved to a period ending in March and made a one-time exception credit for that first transition year.
external_disconnect: Required (per DEC interconnection forms terminology distinguishing 'Non-Export' agreements from 'Net Metering' agreements)
non_export_option: Yes -- DEC's <100kW 'Non-Export' interconnection agreement path appears to function as DEC's defined non-export/limited-export track, distinct from full net metering
grid_charging_allowed: Unclear -- not independently confirmed whether DEC credits or restricts grid-charging of the battery storage systems covered by its supplemental Battery Storage Interconnection Application
storage_specific_notes: Requires supplemental Battery Storage Interconnection Application whenever storage is paired with a generating system; maintains a distinct <100kW Non-Export interconnection track separate from Net Metering and Battery Storage agreements.

utility_name: Delaware Municipal Electric Corp (DEMEC) - member municipal utilities
rule_summary: DEMEC is a joint-action wholesale power agency representing 9 Delaware municipal electric departments (New Castle, Newark, Middletown, Smyrna, Clayton, Dover, Milford, Seaford, Lewes); each member municipality sets its OWN net-metering/interconnection tariff and is exempt from PSC rules per 26 Del. C. Section 1014's cooperative/municipal carve-out, though DEMEC coordinates policy across members. Nonresidential cap is 500 kW per meter (same tier as DEC). Following SB 298 (2022): excess kWh credits revert to the utility (no payout, no rollover) at the end of each member's annualized billing period; DEMEC's recommended (and most members') practice is an annualized period running spring-to-spring so summer-generated credits carry through winter consumption (contrast with DE Electric Coop's rockier transition, and with Delmarva which lets customers choose their own true-up month). Non-residential net-metering customers pay the full reasonable cost of any new/replacement net meter; residential customers pay up to $200 -- statewide statutory floor, but METER COST is billed directly to the customer at DEMEC members (verify this is not absorbed by any individual member as a local incentive). Utilities may consider system reliability/safety/capacity when reviewing interconnection and net-metering applications (SB 298), giving DEMEC members discretion PSC-regulated Delmarva may have less of.
external_disconnect: Not independently confirmed this pass (varies by individual member municipality)
storage_specific_notes: Each of the 9 member municipalities (Newark, Milford, Seaford, Smyrna, Dover, Lewes, Middletown, Clayton, New Castle) may have its own interconnection agreement text and minor local variations -- treat this row as the DEMEC-coordinated baseline, not a guarantee that every member is identical; confirm against the specific municipality's own utility department before finalizing a project in that territory.

rule_summary: Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps (2MW / 200% baseline / 3,000 MW aggregate). BGE was a lead participant in the 2019-2024 PSC Energy Storage Pilot Program (SB 573): built a 2.5 MW / 7.1 MWh lithium-ion BESS at its Fairhaven substation (winter peak support + PJM frequency regulation) and a 2 MWh project at Chesapeake Beach. Pilot concluded December 2024 -- outputs now feed into the 2025 PSC pilot interim report and inform BGE's participation in the newer DRIVE Act EDSSS pilot (customer-sited battery/bidirectional-EV compensation, up to ~$300/kW-yr, per 7/1/2025 Commission directive). BGE recovers community-solar/net-metering bill credits via its decoupling mechanism (distribution) plus SOS energy cost adjustment (transmission/energy) -- a BGE-specific cost-recovery detail not shared by all MD IOUs.
storage_specific_notes: Fairhaven (2.5MW/7.1MWh) and Chesapeake Beach (2MWh) utility-owned pilot BESS assets are grid-services projects, not customer-facing BYOD -- distinguish from the DRIVE Act EDSSS pilot, which IS customer-sited-storage-facing and the closer match to a 'BYOD' concept at BGE.

rule_summary: Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps. Pepco's PSC storage pilot project: 1.05 MW / 4.25 MWh BESS at National Harbor (substation deferral, peak shaving, reliability); Pepco retains contractual right to draw up to 3 MWh over a 3-hour period, up to 10 days/year, over a 10-year period -- i.e. a partially utility-dispatchable asset even though it may be sited to also serve local reliability. Pepco MD is also the lead/largest DRIVE Act EDSSS pilot utility by targeted capacity (~185 MW combined target across BGE/PHI/Potomac Edison per 2025 filings, Pepco MD's own VPP target ~185 MW noted in programs.csv separately for Pepco MD specifically).
storage_specific_notes: National Harbor BESS has a utility call-option structure (10 days/yr, 3hrs, up to 3MWh) rather than being a pure customer-storage-facing BYOD program.

rule_summary: DC-specific delta from the DC state row: Pepco is the sole electric distribution company in DC, so DC state rules and Pepco DC's tariff are effectively identical -- no further utility-level deviation identified beyond what's captured in the DC state row (100kW cap, 1:1 retail NEM, indefinite rollover, December cash-out of remaining NEG at generation rate only). DC's SREC market ($360-400/MWh range cited in 2026 secondary sources) interacts with storage in that AC-coupled storage added to an existing SREC-generating solar system generally does not itself generate SRECs (SRECs track solar production, not storage throughput) -- verify metering configuration required to avoid inadvertently affecting SREC certification when retrofitting storage onto an existing DC solar system.
storage_specific_notes: Retrofit caution: adding storage to an existing SREC-certified system may require DOEE review of metering configuration to preserve SREC eligibility -- not independently confirmed against DOEE rules this pass, flagged as a retrofit risk worth checking case-by-case.

rule_summary: Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps. Potomac Edison's PSC storage pilot built TWO projects (broader than the single-project norm among the other three pilot utilities): a 1.75 MW / 8.4 MWh BESS in Little Orleans (Allegany/Washington County, backup power for 1,000+ customers during outages, built with Convergent Energy and Power, online ~Jan 2025) and a 500 kW battery at the Myersville Park & Ride (Frederick County, bundled with EV fast chargers to study demand-spike mitigation). Potomac Edison also uniquely still applies community-solar credits as a kWh USAGE REDUCTION on subscriber bills rather than a dollar credit (per PSC's Nov 2025 net metering report) -- transitions to dollar-credit method 1/1/2026, a live utility-specific billing-mechanics change relevant to any MD savings modeling tool.
storage_specific_notes: Little Orleans and Myersville are utility-owned/co-developed grid-reliability BESS assets (not customer BYOD); Potomac Edison's community-solar billing mechanic (kWh reduction vs. dollar credit) changes 1/1/2026 -- update any hardcoded MD billing-treatment assumption after that date.

rule_summary: SMECO is a cooperative but, unlike Delaware's DEC, MD's COMAR 20.50 net metering/interconnection rules are written to bind 'electric companies' inclusive of cooperatives -- SMECO's PSC Net Metering Report data (avg. April 2025 credit $58.08 across 3,612 residential accounts) is reported alongside the IOUs under the same statewide cap/sizing framework, with no distinct SMECO-specific cap or sizing deviation identified. NOT independently confirmed among the four utilities that filed 2020 PSC storage pilot proposals (BGE, Pepco, Delmarva, Potomac Edison) -- SMECO does not appear to have participated in the utility-owned storage pilot program, which may mean SMECO territory has less utility-side storage infrastructure/experience than the four Exelon/FirstEnergy utilities, though this is an inference, not a confirmed absence.
storage_specific_notes: No SMECO-specific storage tariff or BYOD program identified in sources reviewed this pass -- if SMECO customers want compensated storage participation, the DRIVE Act EDSSS pilots (BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison) do NOT appear to include SMECO; verify directly with SMECO before assuming parity.

rule_summary: Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 net metering caps/sizing. Choptank publishes its own supplemental interconnection capacity guidance: individual interconnections are restricted to no larger than 3 MVA on 12kV circuits and 5 MVA on 25kV circuits -- a circuit-voltage-class-based ceiling ABOVE the state's 2MW net-metering cap itself, relevant mainly to larger C&I/grid-supply projects seeking non-net-metered interconnection or exceeding net-metering-eligible size. Choptank markets aggregation, solar, net metering, AND energy storage together on a single program page, suggesting more explicit co-op-level support/guidance for storage-paired systems than some peers.
storage_specific_notes: Choptank's marketing groups 'Solar, Net Metering, Aggregation & Energy Storage' together -- suggests an established storage-interconnection pathway, but specific grid-charging/non-export terms not independently retrieved this pass (page required JavaScript, could not fetch full text).

rule_summary: Municipal utility; follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps/sizing but reports its own local net-metered solar capacity: 3.49 MW installed as of 6/30/2025 (per PSC Net Metering Report). No charge to install a net meter at Easton (a favorable deviation vs. utilities that pass through meter costs). Easton allows aggregate NEM combining a single host account with child accounts under the statewide aggregation rules for agricultural/municipal/nonprofit entities.

Follows MD statewide COMAR 20.50 caps. Delmarva's PSC storage pilot is notably different in character from BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison's substation-scale utility-owned BESS: Delmarva contracted with Sunverge Energy to deploy BEHIND-THE-METER residential battery systems in 110 homes in Elk Neck, networked together to function as a virtual power plant (aggregated 0.5 MW / 1.5 MWh). This IS the closest match in the MD pilot program to a customer-sited/BYOD-style storage model referenced in the research brief -- distinguish from BGE/Pepco/Potomac Edison's utility-owned substation/grid-asset pilots, which are NOT customer-owned-device programs.
storage_specific_notes: Elk Neck VPP (Sunverge, 110 homes, 0.5MW/1.5MWh aggregated) is the pilot most resembling a BYOD/customer-storage model in MD; confirm current operational status and whether it has a successor commercial program before assuming it's still active as of 2026.
